title: The simile of the saw
hook: even if bandits sawed you limb from limb, keep a mind of goodwill (MN 21)

segments.voice: Yesterday: crowbar, the fifth tool, force kept for last. Your line: a tool kept for last.

A monk named Moliya Phagguna spent a great deal of time with the nuns. When anyone criticized the nuns in front of him, he got angry and argued. When anyone criticized him in front of them, they got angry and argued. Word of it reached the Buddha. And what he said, first to Phagguna and then to all the monks, builds to a sentence that is hard to hear.
screen: `PHAGGUNA, QUICK TO DEFEND.` → `CRITICISM, THEN ANGER.` → `A HARD SENTENCE.`

segments.voice: MN 21, the Kakacupama. The Buddha tells Phagguna: whatever anyone says, about the nuns or about you, train like this. My mind will not be changed. I won't utter harsh words. I'll stay compassionate, with a mind of goodwill, without inner hate. Then he lays out five ways people may speak to you: at the right time or the wrong time, truly or falsely, gently or harshly, helpfully or not, with goodwill or with hate. Any of the five may come; the training stays the same. Then pictures, one after another. A man comes with a hoe and a basket to make the great earth not-earth. He digs, he scatters, he spits. He can't do it; the earth is too vast. So abide with a mind like the earth: vast, exalted, measureless, without hostility. Someone tries to paint pictures on empty space; there's nothing for the paint to cling to. Someone tries to boil the river Ganges with a blazing grass torch. Someone rubs a soft, well-cured catskin bag and tries to make it crackle. None of it works. And last, the hard sentence. Even if bandits were to cut you apart, limb by limb, with a two-handled saw, whoever let their mind turn to hate because of it would not be carrying out the teaching. It's the extreme case, set at the end as the floor. The Dhammapada says it in an old line, in Max Müller's translation: “hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love.”
screen: `FIVE WAYS PEOPLE MAY SPEAK.` · `A MIND LIKE THE EARTH.` · `PAINT ON SPACE, BURN THE GANGES.` · `EVEN WITH A SAW: NO HATE.` · then, large: `A MIND LIKE THE EARTH.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who criticizes you, not the worst one, someone manageable, and notice what the body does. Then picture the earth under you, wide and unbothered, taking footsteps and rain alike, and see if you can wish that critic one ordinary good thing, like a good night's sleep. If you can't today, that's honest; the earth can wait.
Kakacupama, the simile of the saw. Even under the cruelest treatment, keep a mind of goodwill, vast and steady as the earth.
Your line: a mind like the earth. Wide enough that a sharp word has room to land. That's day four hundred seventeen.

howItsDone: Teachers cite the simile of the saw when they teach patience, and some pair it with loving-kindness meditation directed toward difficult people.

fork.setup: someone tries to boil the river Ganges with a blazing grass torch. what happens, in MN 21?
options: nothing: the river is far too vast
fork.reveal: the torch can't touch it. a mind made vast with goodwill is like that: the harsh word has nothing to burn.

original.note: Pali kakacūpama: the simile of the saw; kakaca is a saw.

trapdoor: what you thought: be nice even to bandits.
what it means: a mind so wide and steady, like the earth, that cruelty can't turn it to hate.
what a scholar hears: kakaca is a saw, and the Pali specifies a two-handled one; the same sutta also tells the story of the housewife Vedehikā and her maid.
recall: taints: what flows in the mind

chat.says: Someone at work keeps criticizing me. Am I allowed to hate them a little?
options: MN 21 says keep a mind like the earth, with goodwill, however you're spoken to.
Yes, if the criticism is unfair, a little ill will is fully allowed.
No, but only because hating them might hurt your reputation at work.
chat.meaning: In MN 21, whether speech is true or false, gentle or harsh, the training stays the same: a mind of goodwill, vast as the earth.
